correctness.rationale: If a peripheral path starts wholly white, the hub has two permanently white neighbors in that petal and no first force can enter. This also forces hub inclusion because a connected set omitting it lies in a single petal. With the hub selected, connectedness is precisely the prefix/suffix restriction; any nonempty pattern spreads through its one possible white gap independently. Thus petal coefficients are s+1 for proper selections of size s>0 and 1 for the full selection, giving the stated product, interval of degrees and extremal coefficients. Each petal has positive log-concave coefficients and the classical no-internal-zero convolution theorem applies. The c>=5 real-zero exclusion follows by normalizing the first three coefficients to 1,3/2,2: for all-negative roots the square of the first nonconstant coefficient would exceed twice the next coefficient, but 9/4<4. Small factors split. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 2; 47 bouquets with 2–4 petals of lengths 3–7 and order at most 13, 149681 nonempty masks per pass, counting connected sets that hit all minimal forts and comparing exact polynomials. The two-direction fort-hitting equivalence follows from first entry and the stalled white set; finite checks do not prove the general results.

value.rationale: Bouquets are a natural multicycle cactus family with independent petal choices. The result gives uniform shape in a setting where connected-forcing sequences are not unimodal in general, and pinpoints the precise coexistence of log-concavity with nonreal roots rather than inferring one from the other. This is valuable as a coefficient-shape theorem, not as an assertion of new cactus minimum-set structure.
